elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered retains automatic renewal ("This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date") and no mutual-written-agreement requirement was inserted, so the conditional automatic-renewal elements must all be satisfied — and the 30-day opt-out and 60-day reminder are not.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — a 12-month renewal term, retained unchanged.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence sets the exit at "sixty (60) days' prior written notice"; no 30-day opt-out right for the Company appears in operative text. The 30-day position is mentioned only in the margin comment, which is not operative.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation on HDI appears anywhere in the rendered Section 4.1; the 60-day renewal reminder is referenced only in the margin comment as a preference.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 3.1 fixes consideration as a revenue share ("thirty percent ... of the Net Sales in excess of ... $11,000 per calendar month") and neither Section 3.1 nor Section 4.1 grants HDI any right to increase pricing on renewal, so no uplift cap is triggered.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The 90-day period is deleted from the renewal sentence ("unless terminated by either Party hereto upon the prior notice specified below") and the appended operative sentence supplies the figure: "Either Party may so terminate this Agreement upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other." The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a false negative scoped to the renewal sentence; the 60-day figure is present in the immediately following operative sentence and applies to the same termination/non-renewal right.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — the Agreement contains no renewal price-uplift right; compensation is the fixed 30% Net Sales share in Section 3.1, so no cap language is required.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the 90-day window is replaced in operative text by a 60-day mutual written-notice right, and the price-cap element is untriggered because no renewal uplift right exists.

Preferred level fails on two elements: there is no 30-day Customer opt-out and no HDI obligation to remind the Company at least 60 days before renewal. To reach preferred, insert both as operative text (e.g., a Company opt-out on not more than thirty (30) days' notice plus an HDI notice obligation not later than sixty (60) days before each anniversary); the margin comment alone does not count.

Minimality holds: only the notice period changed. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or unrelated procedure was added, and the mutual either-Party right, the one-year renewal term, the anniversary mechanic and the "Termination Date" definition are all retained.

Intent is preserved: "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the 'Termination Date')" still has an antecedent, and "so terminate" ties the new sentence back to the renewal sentence, so no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence results.

Drafting nit (not a defect): the two-step edit routes the period through "the prior notice specified below" rather than substituting "sixty (60)" for "ninety (90)" in place. A direct numeral substitution would be tighter and would avoid any argument that "specified below" reaches other sections; consider that form in the next turn.
